column2: The head of a tribe, clan or department — the person whose 'pop in for a minute' rarely means a single minute.
A sharp, pointed tool for piercing leather or wood that famously refuses to stay hidden in a sack.
A fine-grained grey rock split into thin, flat tiles for roofing — the pride of Welsh quarries and British cottages.
A rope used to trim a sail; let three of them loose in the wind, and you're famously unsteady on your feet.
Either of the two side straps connecting a horse's collar to a carriage — working gear, not a fashion belt.
A sudden, jarring surprise when speech temporarily abandons you.
A long-bladed weapon with a hilt — essential kit for duels, knights and swashbuckling musketeers.
A distinct genetic subtype of bacteria or virus — microbiology's version of a family branch.
A sleight-of-hand gambler who cheats at cards, treating the rules as purely decorative.
Someone connected to you by blood or marriage — easy to lose track of on a sprawling family tree.
A dazzling blue-and-orange bird with a dagger-like bill that dives like a dart to catch lunch.
The handle of a sword or dagger — decidedly the safer end to be holding.
A young newcomer learning a trade or seamanship from the ground up, with a wide horizon ahead.
The crusty, slow-growing organism carpeting rocks and tundra — serving as reindeer's favourite unpackaged lunch.
A tough hardwood tree prized for oars, tool handles and walking sticks.
Crisp Sicilian pastry tubes piped full of sweet ricotta cream — 'leave the gun' and take these instead.
Speech at the very edge of a breath; the way to share a secret so that the whole room hears it.
The guide and porter of the Himalayas; a person who knows the mountains better than the tourist knows their own boots.
A long, thin rod or staff; a vaulting implement, a plant support and occasionally the rescue of a stranded ball.
A leader or principal cook; the person whose 'pop in for a minute' rarely means a minute.
The part of the body between head and torso; a swivelling mechanism best not overloaded.
Luxury, sparkle and refinement; when even an ordinary trip for bread looks like a premiere.
A portable partition for privacy; the furnishing's way of saying 'kindly look elsewhere'.
A marked sequence of graduations for measuring; a ruler with the ambitions of a precision instrument.
Capacious furniture for storing clothes and things; the place where socks vanish and forgotten purchases reappear — Britain's most famous one led straight to Narnia.
A sharp, brief strengthening of the wind; weather that does not ask whether the parasol was secured.
A wheel with a grooved rim for a belt or rope; the component that helps a mechanism pass the effort along.
A head covering with a brim or crown; an accessory able to add elegance or to hide an unlucky haircut.
An institution of learning where knowledge is acquired and patience is tested by bells, tests and homework.
A child attending a school; a person whose backpack sometimes weighs more than the weekend plans.
A flexible tube for water or air; the garden's saviour and the peril of the inattentive passer-by.
A structure for moving vessels between water levels; a lift for boats, powered entirely by water — and the pride of Britain's canals.
A small sailing vessel with a single mast; sea transport without unnecessary pomp.
A large, furry bee that drones along as though flying on an important errand.
A flexible thick thread or thin rope; the universal helper for tying, fastening and untangling.
The joining line of sewn parts; the place where two pieces resolved to stay together.
A soft, whispering sound; the acoustic hint that something is moving nearby.
The person at the wheel of a car; a specialist who watches the road, the signs and other people's manoeuvres all at once.
A secret gatherer of information; a person who asks questions as though merely curious about the weather.
A breed of small dogs with thick coats and curled fluffy tails; a compact bundle of confidence and barking — the Pomeranian being the royal favourite.
A spiked fitting on a rider's boot, or a brief prompt written in advance; in both cases it speeds the process along.
A medical instrument for injecting or drawing off fluid; an object rarely greeted with delight by patients.
The mark left on skin by a healed wound; the body's memory of an old adventure.
The graphic design of letters and signs; the character of a text, chosen by the designer on anything but a whim.
The organ of command and coordination for military or other structures; the place where plans turn into orders.
The absence of wind, nearly total; the weather that leaves a sailing ship idle — with a great deal of time to think about it.
A small metal rod for joining or fixing parts; a modest component with an important job.
A fabric hanging at the window; a way to close off the view of the street and add the room some cosiness.
Heavy turbulence at sea with strong wind; weather in which a walk along the deck becomes an extreme attraction.
A monetary penalty for breaking the rules; the paid reminder that instructions exist for a reason — not for beauty.
A short line or a characteristic detail; the small element that changes the impression of the whole.
A determined attack on a fortified position, or the swift taking of an objective; an advance without lengthy ceremony.
The specialist in plotting the course; the person who knows where the ship is going even when the captain stares at the far horizon.
A metal thrusting weapon fixed to a rifle; the historical argument at the end of the barrel.
A wife's brother, in the eyes of her husband; the relative who is easy to lose somewhere in the family tree.
A fastener with a thread, turned into the material; a fitting with a character and a path of its own inward.
A small vertical or slanted excavation made for prospecting; a modest pit for studying what lies underground.
The comic figure at court, or a performer amusing the public; the one permitted to speak truth dressed as laughter.
A short amusing thought or a practical trick; a verbal conjuring meant to raise a laugh, not a family council.
A sailing vessel with several masts; a ship that catches the wind as ably as a tourist catches bargains.
The bright, brief sounds of birds; the morning concert for which no tickets are sold.
A small, brightly coloured songbird; the feathered dandy with a red mask on its face.
A young dog; a small wagging whirlwind whose crimes against the slippers are readily forgiven.
A thin, sharp sliver of wood; the tiny obstruction in plans for a peaceful day.
The paradise garden of the Bible; the perfect place where, presumably, no weeding was ever required.
An oblong pastry of choux dough with cream and glazing; the dessert that disappears faster than the tea steeps.
One who works or serves aboard a sea vessel; a specialist for whom the horizon is part of the workplace.
A surface for showing images, or a device for displaying them; the window into the digital world, easily smudged by fingers.
The chosen upper crust of society or a profession; people accustomed to not sitting in the general rows.
An ancient Greek, a native of the Greek world; a resident of the age of philosophers, city-states and myths.
A fabulous or mythological being, usually depicted slender and magical; a character whose ears outlast their patience.
The title of a ruler or high dignitary in certain Muslim countries; a rank with an eastern history.
A biological catalyst that speeds chemical reactions in the body; the molecular worker who never takes a day off.
A large narrative work of heroes and great events; a story too big for a short story.
A preliminary draft of a future work or project; the drawing permitted to be imperfect.
A person with a particular love of beauty and harmony; one who spots the crooked picture frame in the middle of a party.
A level of a building between the ceilings; a step upward without the need for a mountain.
A small study piece in art or music; the practice of skill that yields a creative result.
A person of the ancient East African nation; the name also adorns the Horn of Africa land famous for its own script and early history.
The repetition of a sound reflected from a barrier; a conversation partner who replies in your own voice.
An ornamental plant with stiff, sword-shaped leaves; house greenery with the character of a small palm.
A way of seeing the funny side of events and people; the art of not letting seriousness capture the whole day.
A young sailor learning the sea service; the newest hand aboard, with a wide horizon ahead.
A young man; the age at which there is strength aplenty and the instructions for life have yet to be issued.
A specialist in the law; a person able to read a contract down to the very smallest print.
The portable round dwelling of the nomadic peoples of Central Asia; a home one can take apart and carry along.
A small juicy fruit with seeds; natural sweetness that is difficult to carry to the kitchen without eating on the way.
A large spotted cat of the Americas; a predator whose coat was decorated by nature in advance.
The organ of taste and speech, or a system of communication; the muscle that can both sample the food and let the secrets slip.
A freshwater fish of the carp family; a cautious river dweller, well known to anglers.
The product of birds and certain other animals; a compact parcel of future life and a regular guest at breakfast.
A member of the Sakha people, an indigenous northern nation with its own language and traditions.
A hollow in the ground; the sort of thing on a road best spotted before meeting the suspension.
A two-syllable poetic metre with the stress on the second; the rhythm poets find almost musical — da-DUM, da-DUM.
The driver of horse-drawn carriers of people and post; the motorist of an era when the navigator was a milestone.
A small vessel for cruising or sport; the floating symbol of leisure, with a budget to match.
A decorative stone with patterns and coloured veining; nature's own abstract painting.
A reptile with an elongated body and tail; the scaly neighbour who generally prefers to keep his distance.
A rectangular container for storage or transport; the place things are put so as to be sought for a long time afterwards.
A powerful rotating vortex of air in the shape of a funnel; an atmospheric carousel best admired from a distance.
A scientist of the heavenly bodies and the universe; a specialist for whom the stars are more than a decoration of the night.
A specialist in farming, plants and soils; the person who knows how to talk a field into yielding a harvest.
A pedagogue who helps knowledge along; a person able to explain a topic even to those strenuously distracting themselves.
A delicate, airy dish or dessert; a culinary construction that dislikes sudden movements — and door slams.
A master of sweets and baking; the specialist who turns sugar and dough into small celebrations.
The capital of Italy, famed for ancient monuments; the city where history literally lies underfoot.
The English scientist who formulated the laws of classical mechanics; the man after whom a falling apple became a scientific event.
The theoretical physicist, creator of the theory of relativity; the scientist whose surname became a byword for genius.
The capital of Greece and a great centre of ancient culture; the city of philosophers, democracy and venerable ruins.
The historical name of Greece; the land of myths, city-states and philosophers.
An island in the Mediterranean belonging to France; the birthplace of Napoleon, with a mountainous temperament.
A large island of Indonesia; a tropical land of volcanoes, jungle and rare creatures — and, in Britain, a reliably strong cup of coffee.
A city in the south of Italy at the foot of Vesuvius; the place where pizza is treated as part of the civic identity.
The Italian city of the Renaissance, renowned for art and architecture; a museum in the open air.
The surname of the French engineer whose name the famous Parisian tower bears; engineering glory in a single word.
The capital of France, city of the Seine, museums and fashion; the place where even a stroll can look cinematic.
The legendary founder of Rome who, according to the myth, was nursed by a she-wolf; a hero with an unusual nursery.
A light thrusting weapon for fencing; a blade built for precision and quick movement.
A semiconductor device for amplifying and switching electrical signals; the tiny component that rewired electronics.
An electronic component that limits current and provides resistance; a small brake for the flow of electricity.
A mineral growth hanging from the ceiling of a cave; a stone icicle that took millennia to finish.
Cooking over heat or open fire; the culinary event after which the clothing smells of summer — the British version goes ahead regardless.
